22. The homogeneous model of the universe predicts that it may be considered as a spherical cloud of matter of radius $r$ and uniform density $\rho$. Consider a particle of mass $m$ at the edge of the universe moving with velocity $v$ and obeying Hubble's law.
[Diagram: sphere of radius $r$ with a particle of mass $m$ on its surface moving outward with velocity $v$]
(a) Justify that the total energy of this particle is $E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{4}{3}\pi G\rho r^2 m$. [2]
(b) At critical density there is zero total energy. Show that the critical density of the universe is: $\rho_c = \frac{3H_0^2}{8\pi G}$. [2]
(c) The accepted value for the Hubble constant is $2.3 \times 10^{-18}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. Estimate the critical density of the universe. [1]
questions.review_note: In the source PDF the Greek rho in (a) and (b) renders as a plain r glyph; transcribed as rho.
